CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not fire first with new tariffs or non-tariff measures. Open and keep a formal channel on the pending Section 301 IP/tech-transfer case and the February Section 232 steel/aluminum recommendations, while taking the January Section 201 solar/washer safeguards to the WTO with other affected members. Offer talks and limited commercial packages if they buy time, but make no structural IP, JV, or Made-in-China-2025 concessions before Washington has issued 301 findings or decided 232. Quietly prepare retaliation lists so a later mirror response is ready if 301/232 land hard.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but still prospective, not existential. The live hit is the 22 January 2018 Section 201 action (30% solar safeguard declining over four years; washer TRQs), which MOFCOM called an abuse of remedies and which lands on a sector China dominates after earlier AD/CVD evasion. That is a material export-sector wound, not a systemic shock. The larger threat is the unfinished campaign: the 14 August 2017 Section 301 investigation into forced tech transfer, JV/equity limits, outbound tech acquisition, and cyber-enabled IP theft—explicitly tied to industrial-policy goals—and the 16 February 2018 Commerce 232 options that name China for a 53% steel tariff basket and a 23.5% aluminum tariff. January 2018 reporting already said USTR might be considering large unilateral 301 tariffs. The November 2017 Beijing visit produced MOUs, not structural IP relief, so commercial deal-making alone will not close the case. Macro data as of late February do not show the dispute biting China: industrial production ~7.2% YoY, seasonally adjusted merchandise exports up sharply into February, reserves still ~$3.15tn, and CNY stronger (about 6.32 per dollar vs ~6.63 in October). No FX stress, no firm-level entity listing, no unemployment signal in export hubs. That combination—opening U.S. salvo plus a multi-statute campaign being assembled, against a still-healthy Chinese economy—sits between neutral and the +0.5 “major export sectors hit / FX pressure” anchor, hence +0.28. Action should stay near zero: preemptive escalation would give Washington cover to choose the harshest 232 option and to treat 301 as already answered, while full concession or purchase commitments are premature because there is no 301 determination and no matching U.S. offer. Negotiate without new commitments, use the WTO on 201, and hold fire until the April 232 clock and the 301 record force a clearer choice.
key_factors: Section 201 solar/washer safeguards already in force (22 Jan 2018); China protested as WTO-inconsistent overreaction
Section 301 IP/tech-transfer investigation open since Aug 2017; no findings yet, but Jan 2018 reports of possible large unilateral tariffs
Commerce 232 recommendations (16 Feb 2018) include China-specific steel (53%) and aluminum (23.5%) options; presidential decision due mid-April
Nov 2017 Beijing summit produced commercial MOUs, not structural IP/tech-transfer concessions
China macro still healthy: IP ~7.2% YoY, strong exports, ~$3.15tn reserves, CNY appreciating — dispute not yet in the real economy
Preemptive retaliation would waste leverage and political positioning before 301/232 land; structural concessions are premature

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump signs memorandum directing USTR to investigate China's IP and technology-transfer practices under Section 301. USTR investigation initiated.
Trump visits Beijing; large package of commercial deals announced (many MOUs). No substantive concessions on structural IP / tech-transfer issues.
Trump approves Section 201 safeguard tariffs on solar panels and washing machines (China among suppliers hit). First major tariff action of the administration.
China industrial production index 107.2 as of 2018-02-01 (~7.2% YoY); still expanding, no dispute-driven contraction.
China merchandise exports (SA) 253.3bn USD in Feb 2018, up sharply over the 180-day window — export engine not yet impaired.
China total reserves ex-gold ~3.15 trillion USD in Feb 2018; ample buffer, no reserve-drain crisis.
CNY strengthened from 6.6254 (Oct 2017) to 6.3183 (Feb 2018); no FX pressure from the dispute.
China MOFCOM branded the Section 201 move an overreaction and abuse of trade remedies; pledged to work with other WTO members to protect its interests.

Jan 2018: USTR 301 findings due by Aug 2018, but reporting said the investigation may already be done and the administration was considering significant tariffs, with some talk of damage estimates in a very large range.

16 Feb 2018: Commerce 232 options include 24% global steel tariff or 53% on 12 countries including China, and 7.7% global aluminum or 23.5% on China/HK/Russia/Venezuela/Vietnam; Trump must decide by mid-April.
